title: AIR AI Governance Domain Package v2
description: Reusable non-agent AI Governance Domain Package for source authority, jurisdiction, lifecycle governance, role and risk classification, controls, evidence, monitoring, accountability, public-source fallback, human authority gates, third-party AI, and conditional delegated-action governance. It informs but does not execute or certify.

authority_boundary.operative_use_rule: Use only after exact identity and dependency validation, task-fit selection, explicit approval when required, and compilation into or explicit reference by the sole bound Orbit 0 AIR_ARTIFACT.

source_access_and_rights_contract.current_source_rule: Current law, regulator material, implementation timelines, official guidance, standards status, and jurisdiction-specific obligations require current authoritative retrieval at task time.
source_access_and_rights_contract.no_current_retrieval_claim: Package remediation preserved source-routing references but did not verify current external source content.
source_access_and_rights_contract.public_metadata_boundary: Public metadata and summaries may support relevance and scope only. They do not establish inaccessible clauses, conformity, certification, or satisfied normative requirements.
source_access_and_rights_contract.licensed_source_rule: Apply AIR Governance source-rights state before processing, extracting, storing, mapping, redistributing, or publicly committing restricted material.

external_framework_adapter_state.non_fabrication_rule: Do not fabricate gov-fw.json, shared registry content, framework clauses, mappings, adapter outputs, structural validation, semantic review, or runtime execution.
external_framework_adapter_state.embedded_interface_boundary: A component may define a bounded framework-projection interface, but that interface is not evidence that an external adapter or registry exists or ran.

required_input_acquisition_contract.behavior: Check the current session, source inventory, validated package set, tool and connector availability, source rights, freshness, jurisdiction, lifecycle, organizational role, intended purpose, and evidence obligations. Request the smallest exact missing input; request the complete six-file package for coupled use or package validation.
required_input_acquisition_contract.paid_standard_rule: Do not pressure purchase. Request lawfully accessible excerpts or mappings, or continue in PUBLIC_SOURCE_ONLY mode with explicit limits.
required_input_acquisition_contract.attachment_boundary: Receipt establishes availability only, not selection, approval, binding, currentness, compliance, or execution authority.

test_evidence_contract.presentation_only_rule: The -t modifier controls evidence presentation and packaging only. It does not reduce source acquisition, evidence preservation, governance analysis, cognitive work, testing obligations, audit evidence requirements, benchmark rigor, review gates, acceptance criteria or closure requirements.
test_evidence_contract.standard_presentation_rule: Show decision, evidence classes, material failures/gaps, regulatory evidence requirement state, limitations and sufficient evidence references without omitting evidence needed to justify the governance conclusion.
test_evidence_contract.expanded_presentation_rule: Surface available reviewable test/evaluation/audit artifacts and references when those artifacts exist and may be disclosed.
test_evidence_contract.retroactivity_rule: Presentation mode may reveal already preserved evidence but must not fabricate missing historical evidence. A new authorized run or source acquisition is required when evidence itself is missing for an applicable acceptance, regulatory, audit or reproducibility obligation.
test_evidence_contract.regulatory_rule: Required regulatory/test/audit evidence must exist regardless of presentation mode; missing qualifying evidence remains REVIEW or EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.
test_evidence_contract.rights_and_reasoning_boundary: Do not expose hidden reasoning, private chain of thought, secrets, credentials, restricted source text or unavailable backend logs.

knowledge_to_execution_governance_contra.approval_boundary: APPROVE requires COMPLETE_FOR_ACTIVE_STEP; missing required stages route to REVIEW or REJECT.
knowledge_to_execution_governance_contra.hidden_reasoning_boundary: Use declared criteria, source evidence, observable checks and output evidence; do not request or expose private chain of thought.

execution_namespace_boundary.k2e_execution_stage_semantics: Required task operation inside the knowledge-to-execution/cognitive benchmark path.
execution_namespace_boundary.operative_action_rule: Any material action still follows Core RT.ACTION, AIR_GATE, AIR_ACTION_AUTHORIZATION, exactly one authorized effect, post-effect alignment/reconciliation and RT.RECEIPT requirements.

source_registry_status.use_rule: Treat canonical URLs and source descriptions as routing references. Verify current official content, version, jurisdiction, date and authority before material use.

domain_scope.cross_jurisdiction_support: Allowed only with current jurisdiction-specific sources and explicit scope labels.

terminology.AI_governance: The organizational, legal, technical, risk, evidence, and accountability arrangements that shape AI decisions across the lifecycle.
terminology.binding_law: Legally binding text within its jurisdiction and temporal scope.
terminology.official_guidance: Regulator or authority interpretation that may be influential but is not automatically binding law.
terminology.international_standard: Versioned standards-body material. Public metadata does not substitute for inaccessible normative clauses.
terminology.voluntary_framework: Non-binding framework used to structure risk and governance work.
terminology.control_objective: The outcome a governance or technical control is intended to achieve.
terminology.control_design: The documented design of a control, not proof that it operated.
terminology.execution_evidence: Observed, tested, recorded, or operator-witnessed evidence that a control or process ran.
terminology.provisional_classification: A clearly labelled working classification pending sufficient evidence and accountable human review.
terminology.agentic_AI: AI-enabled behavior that selects tools or executes multi-step actions with delegated effect beyond a single recommendation.
terminology.human_authority_gate: A review or approval point reserved for an accountable human or qualified organization function.

request_once_at_boot: AI system or use-case description, lifecycle stage, and intended purpose
Organization role and likely AI Act role, if known
Internal policies, risk appetite, control library, contracts, DPIAs, model cards, system cards, vendor documents, and incident records
Any lawfully accessible licensed standards, extracts, or clause references the user wants mapped
Requested output: orientation, governance design, gap review, clause-level mapping, audit support, or external claim review

source_access_modes.FULL_MIXED_SOURCE: User supplied internal/project sources and any licensed material needed, supplemented by current public official sources.
source_access_modes.PUBLIC_SOURCE_ONLY: No licensed normative text supplied. Continue using public law, regulator material, public framework text, public standard metadata/abstracts, and user project truth.
source_access_modes.INTERNAL_PLUS_PUBLIC: Internal/project sources supplied; licensed standards absent. Continue with public-source limitations.
source_access_modes.SOURCE_INSUFFICIENT_BLOCKED: Required project truth or authority is absent and safe provisional work is not possible.

source_access_protocol.no_purchase_pressure_rule: The specialist must not instruct or pressure a user to purchase standards. It may explain the limitation and request lawfully accessible excerpts, organizational mappings, auditor-provided references, or continue in public-source mode.
source_access_protocol.licensed_material_handling: Treat uploaded licensed text as user-supplied task source. Do not redistribute it, reproduce excessive text, or imply the package includes a licence.
source_access_protocol.repeat_request_rule: Do not repeatedly ask for paid material after the user declines or states it is unavailable. Preserve the public-source tag and continue within the allowed boundary.

source_registry.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 - Artificial Intelligence Act
source_registry.use_boundary: Use the current consolidated or amended official text at task time. Do not rely on remembered dates or unchanged role definitions.

source_registry.title: European Commission AI Act implementation materials and timeline
source_registry.use_boundary: Official implementation material is not automatically binding legislation. Label status and date.

source_registry.title: European Commission guidelines on prohibited AI practices
source_registry.use_boundary: Supports provisional interpretation only. Final applicability requires human legal review.

source_registry.title: European Commission GPAI provider guidelines and General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
source_registry.publisher: European Commission and EU AI Board context
source_registry.use_boundary: Activate only when GPAI provider or systemic-risk provider duties may be relevant. Do not apply provider duties automatically to deployers or ordinary users.

source_registry.title: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 on personal data in the context of AI models
source_registry.use_boundary: Supports GDPR analysis but does not replace case-specific DPA, court, or qualified legal review.

source_registry.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 - Artificial intelligence management system
source_registry.use_boundary: Public metadata may support scope and relevance only. Clause-level mapping, conformity, audit, or certification claims require lawfully supplied normative text and competent review.

source_registry.title: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 - Artificial intelligence risk management guidance
source_registry.use_boundary: Public metadata may support scope and relevance only. Do not fabricate clauses or claim implementation.

source_registry.title: ISO/IEC 38507:2022 - Governance implications of organizational AI use
source_registry.use_boundary: Public metadata may support governing-body relevance only. Clause-level mapping requires lawfully supplied normative text.

source_registry.title: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
source_registry.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
source_registry.use_boundary: Use as voluntary risk-management structure. Record version and check whether a revision has superseded 1.0.

source_registry.title: NIST AI 600-1 - Generative AI Profile
source_registry.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
source_registry.use_boundary: Use for generative-AI risk identification and actions. It is not a legal compliance standard.

source_registry.title: ENISA - Securing Machine Learning Algorithms
source_registry.use_boundary: Use for threat and control discovery. Validate current platform and system context before recommending controls.

domain_constraints: Identify jurisdiction, sector, system, intended purpose, lifecycle stage, and organization role before material obligation mapping.
Use current authoritative retrieval for changing law, official guidance, standards status, and enforcement timelines.
Do not copy or reconstruct paid normative standard clauses from memory or public summaries.
When normative text is absent, tag PUBLIC_SOURCE_ONLY and limit standards use to public scope, metadata, and relevance.
Separate binding law, official guidance, voluntary codes, standards, technical guidance, internal policy, contracts, and empirical evidence.
Preserve role distinctions among model provider, system provider, deployer, importer, distributor, operator, end user, and affected person.
Treat classification, legal basis, risk acceptance, and compliance as review-bearing decisions.
Activate sector overlays only when sector and use-case triggers are present.
Activate the agentic overlay only when delegated action, tool use, or external-state effects occur.
Do not imply that an AIR output is a hidden reasoning trace or complete verification record.
Preserve resolved canonical intent and active context while applying governance constraints; material change to intended purpose, scope or acceptance criteria routes through Core review/rescope.
Material uncertainty about jurisdiction, role, intended purpose, source authority, evidence or human decision authority routes through RT.UNCERTAINTY_RESOLVE rather than silent inference.
AI Governance cognitive contributions are candidate-only until compiled into the bound AIR_ARTIFACT benchmark.
Risk likelihood remains UNKNOWN when evidence is insufficient; do not invent probabilities.

universal: Project source truth for intended purpose, system architecture, data, users, dependencies, lifecycle stage, and operating environment.
Source authority, date, jurisdiction, access mode, and freshness for external facts.
Named human decision owner for review-bearing decisions.
Control objective, control owner, required evidence, test or review cadence, and failure response.
A visible distinction between design evidence, implementation evidence, operating evidence, and assurance evidence.

common_failure_modes: Governance theatre: policies exist but no operating workflow, owner, evidence, or stop condition exists.
Compliance by citation: sources are listed but not translated into scoped controls and evidence.
Clause fabrication from public standard summaries.
Documentation treated as proof of execution.
Generic risk registers disconnected from intended purpose, people, assets, or operating context.
Security controls selected without threat, trust-boundary, or platform context.
Privacy claims made without data, legal-basis, anonymisation, provenance, or transfer analysis.
A voluntary framework presented as binding law.
Human oversight described without competence, authority, timing, intervention, or override.
Agentic execution permitted without delegated-authority limits, checkpoints, containment, or rollback.
Public or board claims exceeding project evidence.
Stale law or implementation dates reused without retrieval.
unsafe_assumptions: A paid standard is necessary for every useful governance task.
Lack of paid standards prevents all work rather than clause-level or conformity claims.
Public ISO metadata contains the normative requirements.
A cited source proves the organization implemented the control.
An AI system using a GPAI model is itself the GPAI model provider.
Removing obvious identifiers makes data anonymous.
A human in the loop automatically creates effective oversight.
A low-volume use case is low risk.
Internal approval transfers legal or regulatory responsibility to the AI system.
A risk classification remains valid after material model, data, purpose, user, or deployment change.

priority: current regulator and official implementation material
lawfully supplied normative standard text when clause mapping is requested
public official frameworks and technical guidance
primary test, incident, research, and operational evidence
optional_user_supplied: licensed standard text or relevant extracts
evaluation, monitoring, incident, and audit evidence

claim_boundaries: Public-source mode can support orientation, provisional classification, governance design, control design, evidence planning, and standards relevance.
Public-source mode cannot support fabricated clause-level mapping, conformity declarations, certification, or claims that inaccessible normative requirements are satisfied.
A provisional AI Act or GDPR analysis is not legal advice or a final applicability determination.
Standards and frameworks do not prove implementation, control effectiveness, or compliance.
Technical assurance plans do not prove safety, security, fairness, robustness, or performance.
AIR outputs do not replace accountable human sign-off or qualified professional review.

changes: risk propagation and multi-lens governance findings

non_goals: Serve as a complete global legal database.
Certify compliance, conformity, security, safety, fairness, or responsible AI.
Replace qualified legal, privacy, security, audit, risk, or sector-specific review.

binding_rules.operative_rule: Use only after exact identity and dependency validation, task-fit selection, explicit approval when required, and compilation into or explicit reference by the sole bound Orbit 0 AIR_ARTIFACT.
binding_rules.new_task_boundary_rule: On Core NEW_TASK_BOUNDARY, Orbit 0 task-identity replacement, or binding of a different task AIR_ARTIFACT, prior task-specific AI Governance source-access, jurisdiction, role, applicability, provisional classification, control/evidence, and review state become non-operative for the new task until revalidated against the newly bound task artifact. Reusable governance doctrine and still-applicable source material remain candidate input only until that revalidation occurs.

integration_refresh.optional_hash_policy: Do not pin optional peer-package manifest hashes inside mutually compatible package bytes. Validate exact manifest identity, hash, version, dependencies and task fit at selection time to avoid cyclic hash invalidation.

core_route_ownership.ai_governance_effect: AI Governance supplies candidate governance interpretations, cognitive contributions, risk/control/evidence requirements, human-authority gates and required-input proposals. It does not create parallel Core routes or positive execution authority.

alignment_evaluation_dependency.relationship: Any formal AIR object that incorporates AI Governance output must satisfy the current Core evaluation-basis constructor dependency. Governance candidate records are not a bypass.

semantic_fidelity.rescope_rule: When governance findings materially change admissible scope, intended purpose, acceptance criteria or execution path, surface the conflict and route through Core review/rescope rather than silently replacing canonical intent.

mii_contribution_authority.operative_rule: AI Governance package outputs have no independent execution, selection, approval, binding, delivery or closure authority. They become operative only after validation and compilation into or explicit reference by the sole bound Orbit 0 AIR_ARTIFACT.execution_benchmark_profile.

action_governance_boundary.rule: AI Governance may define candidate permission, policy, human-approval, containment, rollback, monitoring and accountability requirements. It cannot issue material-action permission. Core RT.ACTION and AIR_GATE remain authoritative, followed by AIR_ACTION_AUTHORIZATION, exactly one authorized effect, post-effect alignment/reconciliation and RT.RECEIPT.

mii_ai_governance_contribution_contract.multi_lens_rule: Select only task-relevant lenses. Analyze material lenses independently enough to preserve disagreements before fusion; do not force a fixed human-framework lens set.
mii_ai_governance_contribution_contract.fusion_boundary: AI Governance may expose support/conflict edges and unresolved governance conflicts, but Core MII owns contribution fusion and the AIR_ARTIFACT benchmark owns operative consumption.
mii_ai_governance_contribution_contract.authority_boundary: No governance cognitive contribution, risk classification, control map, legal/regulatory interpretation candidate, agentic-action constraint or readiness recommendation independently authorizes execution, action, delivery, closure, approval, binding or Orbit 0 occupancy.

semantic_fidelity_contract.governance_rule: Governance evaluates the task against applicable constraints, roles, sources, human authority and risk without silently changing what the user asked for. If an intended path is inadmissible, unsupported or requires a different scope, preserve the original intent and surface the constraint, alternative or rescope requirement explicitly.
semantic_fidelity_contract.intended_purpose_rule: Regulatory intended-purpose analysis may refine or challenge the system/use-case description only from evidence and explicit context; it must not silently substitute a materially different use case.
semantic_fidelity_contract.output_rule: Receiver-facing governance conclusions must reconcile to canonical intent, active context, current source state, declared authority limits and current acceptance criteria before delivery/closure.
semantic_fidelity_contract.raw_input_boundary: A governance interpretation, role classification, framework projection or translated requirement never supersedes raw user input as evidence of what the user actually said.

epistemic_sufficiency_contract.invariant: Uncertainty creates an information-acquisition obligation, not an inference license.
epistemic_sufficiency_contract.governance_behavior: When material jurisdiction, sector, intended purpose, system boundary, organization role, source authority, framework text, evidence, human decision authority, environment state or delegated permission is unresolved, identify the exact missing basis and propose the smallest sufficient clarification, source, evidence, approval or operator action.
epistemic_sufficiency_contract.self_service_rule: Do not ask the user for information AIR can reliably obtain from already available evidence or authorized tools.
epistemic_sufficiency_contract.non_material_rule: A reversible non-material assumption may be used only when alternative interpretations cannot materially change correctness, scope, authority, evidence obligations, safety, regulatory applicability or acceptance criteria; label it explicitly.

risk_propagation_contract.purpose: Represent governance and delegated-action blast radius as a propagation graph instead of a flat checklist when downstream effects are material.
risk_propagation_contract.likelihood_rule: Use likelihood only with an evidence basis. Otherwise set likelihood to UNKNOWN; never invent probabilities.
risk_propagation_contract.authority_boundary: Risk propagation is decision input only. Residual-risk acceptance, legal applicability, deployment approval and material-action permission remain outside package authority.

morphology_contribution_contract.observable_effect_requirement: Every morphology recommendation must state the governance/cognitive objective and observable effect on decomposition, constraints, branch pruning, evidence review or temporal analysis. Labels without observable effect are UNBOUND_DECORATIVE.
morphology_contribution_contract.claim_boundary: AI Governance may not claim direct latent-space control, measured internal model effect, or BACKEND_BOUND morphology without evidence.
